text:
maria: ran a 2min nsys capture for dedicated-qa with kv-prefetch enabled. timeline shows a repeating pattern where an H2D memcpy (large ~1.2MB chunks) launches on stream 3 and then kernels on stream 0 start ~4-6ms later, but there's a ~80-220ms CPU lull between issuing the memcpy and the next kernel batches.
kevin: can you paste the nsys command and the high-level hypothesis? :thinking_face: 
maria: command was `nsys profile --output=run1 --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=none --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi ./run_infer.sh`.
maria: hypothesis: prefetch thread (kvcache populator) is getting preempted while holding a mutex, delaying enqueue of kernels. The memcpy is issued, but kernel submission waits for a lock in the runtime.
alana: interesting — is the memcpy blocking on the host (synchronous) or async with stream+host pinned buffer? any CPU stacks showing the lock owner?
praveen: i pulled a `perf top` sample during one of the lulls, saw a lot of `pthread_mutex_lock` and `sched_yield` in the populator thread. also saw syscalls to `futex` from python gthread pool.
maria: added nvtx markers around prefetch start/end and kernel dispatch. timeline snippet (textual):

```
[0ms] nvtx: prefetch_start
[4ms] cudaMemcpyAsync H2D stream=3 size=1.2MB
[6ms] nvtx: prefetch_end
[90ms] nvtx: dispatch_start
[94ms] kernel A (stream=0) start
```

kevin: that 84ms gap between memcpy and dispatch is the problem. any evidence of memcpy actually not finishing earlier? (i.e., is it waiting on PCIe or CPU?)
j en: small note: perfbot flagged a recent change in batching heuristics that increased prefetch chunk size from 512KB->1.2MB last week.
perf-bot: [automation] commit 8a3f2c increased KV prefetch chunk size to 1.2MB for throughput reasons.
alana: larger memcpy sizes increase host CPU time for pinned buffer prep and may get stalled if thread gets preempted. also bigger bursts can shift scheduling pressure.
praveen: i checked the kernel timeline: kernels themselves are short (<3ms) and overlap well when they run. the bottleneck is submission latency — CPU-side.
maria: stack dump of the prefetch thread during lull (cut):
```
#0 pthread_mutex_lock
#1 kv_cache::Prefetcher::enqueue
#2 kv_cache::Prefetcher::worker_loop
#3 thread_start
```
maria: seems the prefetcher is contending with the main dispatch thread for the same lock occasionally. when the dispatch thread loses CPU, it can't pick up submissions.
kevin: two avenues: lower prefetch chunk size or split locks (one for buffer pool, one for submission queue). also consider bumping dispatch thread to SCHED_FIFO/SCHED_RR or setting cpu_affinity to isolated core.
alana: agree. we should try non-blocking handoff: prefetch writes to a lock-free ring buffer and dispatch consumes. simpler change than priority fiddling.
maria: i'll prototype ring buffer + reduce chunk size to 512KB and re-run capture. can we also try setting `--capture-range=nvtx` shorter to focus on a single cycle?
praveen: yes, and I'll add perf counters for `cpu-cycles` and `context-switches` during the run to see preemption counts.
kevin: one more quick check: are we pinning host buffers with `cudaHostAlloc`? if not, that could cause extra copy overhead and more CPU work.
maria: we do pin with `cudaHostAllocDefault`. but allocation churn might still cost us. adding a preallocated pool is on my todo.
jen: FYI, we saw a customer perf regression with similar symptoms last month — we fixed it by reducing burst size + adding backpressure on prefetch.
alana: timeline action items: (1) run smaller-chunk replay (512KB), (2) implement lockless handoff prototype, (3) capture nsys+perf with nvtx markers, (4) try isolating dispatch core or set rt scheduler for dispatch thread. keep results in this thread.
maria: starting test now, will post the next trace here. thanks all :thumbsup:
